title: Player One
description: A full-board tribute to video gaming — classic arcade legends, Nintendo vault classics, iconic characters, famous villains, modern gaming giants, and the moments that shaped the industry.

questions.question: Released by Namco in 1980, this iconic yellow dot-muncher navigates a maze while being chased by four ghosts named Blinky, Pinky, Inky, and Clyde — becoming one of the most recognized video game characters in history.

Released by Taito in 1978, this early arcade game had players defending Earth by shooting at waves of descending pixelated extraterrestrials — establishing the fixed shooter genre and sparking the entire arcade boom of the late 1970s.

In this 1981 Nintendo arcade hit, a plumber named Jumpman climbs girders to rescue a kidnapped woman from a giant ape — introducing the world to a mustachioed hero who would go on to become the most famous character in gaming history.

Capcom's 1991 arcade phenomenon had players choosing from eight distinct fighters — including the fireball-hurling rivals Ryu and Ken — and its head-to-head competitive format defined the fighting game genre and dominated arcade culture throughout the 1990s.

Soviet computer scientist Alexey Pajitnov created this falling-block puzzle game in 1984, but Nintendo's decision to bundle it with the Game Boy in 1989 turned it into a global phenomenon — making it arguably the most-played video game in history.

When Nintendo released this 1985 NES platformer in North America, it almost single-handedly revived the crashed video game market — and its mustachioed Italian plumber remains the most recognizable character in gaming history.

First released on the Super Nintendo in 1992, this Nintendo racing franchise has players hurling shells at each other on colorful tracks — and its brutal Rainbow Road course has been ruining friendships and testing patience for over three decades.

Released for the Nintendo 64 in 1999, this party fighting game was revolutionary for bringing Nintendo's most beloved characters — from the heroic plumber to the electric mouse to the armored bounty hunter — together to battle in one arena.

When players cleared this 1986 Nintendo action-adventure game in under five hours, they received a shocking reveal: the lone armored bounty hunter who had been destroying alien creatures throughout the entire game was, in fact, a woman.

This 1994 Super Nintendo RPG — starring a baseball bat-wielding boy named Ness fighting alien forces across a quirky, modern-day America — was a commercial flop in the US at launch but became one of gaming's most beloved cult classics.

The King of the Koopas and Mario's eternal arch-nemesis, this fire-breathing turtle-lizard hybrid has kidnapped Princess Peach in nearly every game in the franchise since 1985 — and is one of the most recognizable villains in video game history.

The primary antagonist of the Legend of Zelda series, this dark king wields the Triforce of Power, seeks to plunge the land of Hyrule into eternal darkness, and has clashed with the hero Link across over a dozen games spanning four decades.

In Valve's 2007 first-person puzzle game set inside the Aperture Science Enrichment Center, this passive-aggressive artificial intelligence guides the player through increasingly deadly test chambers while delivering darkly funny remarks about science, cake, and their impending death.

In the underwater dystopia of Rapture, this libertarian idealist and founder of the doomed city greets the player via radio throughout a 2007 thriller — culminating in one of gaming's most jaw-dropping villain reveals and the chilling line: 'A man chooses, a slave obeys.'

The self-proclaimed hero of a 2012 looter-shooter RPG set on the chaotic planet of Pandora, this sardonic corporate villain spends the entire game mocking players over the radio — becoming one of gaming's most beloved and expertly written antagonists despite being the main enemy.

Created by Swedish developer Markus 'Notch' Persson and officially released in 2011, this block-building survival sandbox became the best-selling video game of all time — and was purchased by Microsoft in 2014 for $2.5 billion.

Epic Games launched this free-to-play battle royale in 2017, in which 100 players parachute onto an island and fight until only one remains — revolutionizing the industry with its unique building mechanic and generating billions in revenue from cosmetic outfit sales.

Naughty Dog's acclaimed 2013 PlayStation exclusive follows a gruff smuggler named Joel escorting a teenage girl named Ellie across a post-apocalyptic America ravaged by a fungal infection — and is widely regarded as one of the greatest video game stories ever told.
questions.answer: What is The Last of Us?

questions.question: In this 2011 Bethesda open-world RPG, players are the Dragonborn — a legendary warrior who can absorb dragon souls and unleash the thunderous shout 'FUS RO DAH' — free to explore the vast, snow-covered Nordic landscape for hundreds of hours.

FromSoftware's 2011 action RPG became infamous for its brutal difficulty, cryptic storytelling, and the inevitable on-screen message 'YOU DIED' — spawning an entirely new 'Soulslike' genre and a devoted community that considers suffering through it a badge of honor.

Sega created this wise-cracking, sneaker-wearing blue mascot in 1991 as a direct rival to Nintendo's famous plumber — and his blazing speed, spiky silhouette, and attitude made him the defining symbol of the 1990s console wars.

A Spartan warrior who slays the God of War and claims his throne, this PlayStation hero has been one of Sony's biggest icons since 2005 — evolving from a rage-fueled Greek mythology avenger into a measured and protective father figure in the acclaimed Norse-mythology reboot.

This silver-haired, monster-hunting protagonist from CD Projekt Red's fantasy RPG trilogy gained worldwide mainstream recognition with 'The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt' in 2015 — one of the highest-rated games ever made — long before a Netflix adaptation introduced him to an even wider audience.

This charming Renaissance-era Italian assassin from Florence became the breakout star of Ubisoft's 'Assassin's Creed' series, hunting corrupt Templars through the streets of Venice, Rome, and Constantinople across three beloved games between 2009 and 2011.

The quiet, morally conflicted outlaw hero of Rockstar's 2018 epic, this gunslinger navigates the dying days of the American frontier in 1899 — earning widespread praise as one of the most emotionally resonant and fully realized protagonists in video game history.

Released by Atari in 1972, this ridiculously simple simulation of table tennis — two paddles and a bouncing dot — became the first commercially successful video arcade game and quietly launched the entire multi-billion dollar gaming industry.

After a catastrophic market crash in 1983 wiped out the North American video game industry, a Japanese company launched this home console in the US in 1985 — cleverly bundling it with a robotic toy to enter toy stores — and single-handedly revived gaming with the slogan 'Now you're playing with power.'
questions.answer: What is the Nintendo Entertainment System?

questions.question: Released by Atari in 1982 and developed in just five weeks to cash in on the Spielberg blockbuster, this notoriously poor video game adaptation contributed to the North American gaming crash — and millions of its unsold cartridges were famously buried in a New Mexico landfill, confirmed by excavators in 2014.

Nintendo's 1989 handheld revolutionized gaming on the go — launching alongside a falling-block puzzle game that became one of the most-played in history — and sold over 118 million units to become the best-selling portable console of its generation.

Solo developer Eric Barone — working alone under the name ConcernedApe — spent over four years crafting every pixel, note of music, and line of code in this 2016 farming RPG entirely by himself, then released a polished masterpiece that went on to sell over 20 million copies.
